newsitem.title: POLAND: Poison gas spills from oil well near Polish town.
newsitem.headline: Poison gas spills from oil well near Polish town.

text.p: Poisonous hydrogen sulphide gas leaked from an oil and natural gas drill shaft near Debno in western Poland on Thursday but officials said there was no immediate danger to the town of 14,000 people.
A senior civil defence official in the provincial capital Gorzow told Reuters there was also no possibility of any gas reaching the German border, about 20 km (12 miles) from Debno.

The official, who asked not to be named, said gas concentrations were restricted to about 300 metres around the site of the exploratory oil shaft from which the gas had been leaking since morning near Rozansk, six km (four miles) from Debno.

"At present the atmospheric conditions mean the concentrations of gas are stable," police spokeswoman Bozena Stanczyk told Reuters from Gorzow in the early afternoon, adding there was no sign of any reaching Debno.
She said there had been no casualties but children had been evacuated from a school in Rozansk village and adults were ready to follow if the wind changed to blow gas their way.
All fire officers in the province had been mobilised and police were halting traffic into the area around the shaft, while a team from the firm operating it dealt with the leak.
Earlier there were reports that Debno residents could smell the gas and authorities advised them to go to upper floors.

"People should stay at home. If they smell hydrogen sulphide, as they do in Debno, they should go to higher buildings, the second or third floor or higher," local civil defence inspector Stanislaw Smerwinski said on private Radio Zet.
